findings.reason: the one-word normalisation ("G/μ0") is the quantity the convexity and single-root claim depends on, and without it the sentence is dimensionally wrong in exactly the place a worker may take its guard from.
findings.text: the sentence "its symmetric spectrum lies in [0, 1], and the demagnetising operator is positive semidefinite" states the bound of G, but G is the field-per-unit-magnetisation matrix and carries units of μ0 (measured eigenvalues of G/μ0 are 4.9e-5 to 0.99994, i.e. 6.2e-5 to 1.26 in G), so the spectrum statement and the convexity conclusion that now rests on it hold only for G/μ0, as the done-when at line 332 correctly writes — and a guard built from the narrative rather than the done-when would test G's eigenvalues and pass for any physical operator
